A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenDeg work and have readable text, figures, tables and equations. Both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplements, although they refer to supplementary dataset lists, implementation details and additional results. Those materials cannot be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration experiments with NAFNet, PromptIR and Swin, including quantitative comparisons, synthetic-data scaling and domain-gap analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds DA-CLIP and Diff-Plugin training comparisons and Wasserstein-distance measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same conditioning mechanism, structure-correction procedure, degradation sampling and filtering, and Swin restoration architecture. Evaluating GenDS with additional restoration models does not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: The six degradation tasks and all named evaluation benchmarks are retained. However, Figure 2 revises the existing-data composition, particularly motion blur's real/synthetic breakdown. Without the referenced training-dataset lists, it is unclear whether this reflects changed training coverage or corrections to dataset accounting.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2–3 add DA-CLIP and matched Diff-Plugin comparisons trained with and without GenDS, extending the controlled comparison to diffusion-based restorers. The original pretrained Diff-Plugin baseline remains, now marked with #. Figure 1 also replaces PromptIR with Diff-Plugin in its selected comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a Wasserstein-distance evaluation of DA-CLIP degradation-feature distributions, comparing training data with OoD test data and using within-distribution distances as a reference. The existing with/without-GenDS evaluation design is extended to two diffusion restorers; the retained restoration metrics remain LPIPS and FID.

E4.justification: The introduction and new Table 1 add a quantitative check of the OoD designation: the within-distribution mean distance is 0.084, versus OoD distances of 0.173–0.349. The existing scaling, synthetic-only training, degradation-diversity and intensity-control analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial DA-CLIP and Diff-Plugin results in both evaluation regimes. For example, its DA-CLIP O-Haze LPIPS/FID entries are 0.369/154.6 without GenDS and 0.251/113.7 with GenDS. It also adds Wasserstein results and revises Figure 2 annotations, including the haze scene-count increase from 1619% to 1503%. All original restoration-table entries and Figure 6 scaling values are retained.

T1.justification: The degradation-statistics definitions and Equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. The new Wasserstein measurement is an empirical diagnostic, without an added mathematical derivation, formal property or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: controllable degradation synthesis, approximately 550k generated samples and 750k GenDS samples, and improved OoD restoration. Testing additional models strengthens the evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new feature-distance measurements as validation of its OoD designation and directly uses trained Diff-Plugin results to support applicability to generative restoration. Existing explanations and limitations concerning scene diversity, structure-correction failures and synthetic/real alignment remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes the publicly available pretrained Diff-Plugin model from the authors' training comparisons. It removes v1's promise that code will be made publicly available while retaining the project-page link; this does not establish a change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds AWRaCLe and distinctions from DreamBooth, distribution matching distillation and EPE. References for BLIP-2 and two deraining works are also added. These provide additional context while retaining the main novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Prose is tightened throughout the introduction, related work, methods and analyses. The author block is consolidated and acknowledgments become unnumbered, while the section sequence and overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds a compact Wasserstein table and expands both restoration tables. Figure 1 changes selected models, axes and legends; the t-SNE and scaling plots are redrawn or relabelled, with Figure 6 enlarged. These are localized display revisions within the retained layout; the architecture diagram and qualitative image panels remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through controlled comparisons with two diffusion restorers and a quantitative check of OoD separation. These additions support the existing generalization claim beyond the earlier three non-generative models. The improvement remains limited by unavailable supplementary experimental details and unexplained revisions to Figure 2's dataset accounting.
